title: Define module ownership and runtime integration points
purpose: Create a module map that makes each runtime responsibility testable and prevents duplicate execution stacks.
scope: Map AgentCore, Planner, ModelBroker, Memory, Scheduler, ObservationProcessor, ToolRouter, PolicyEvaluator, CapabilityManager, SandboxExecutor, AuditJournal, RollbackManager, RecoveryReconciler, and TUI.
Define stable Rust module locations and public interfaces.
Define which modules may write audit events and which may only request event writes.
Define CLI/API integration points for running, inspecting, approving, and recovering Agent runs.
Identify modules that remain stubbed in this workflow versus implemented.
deliverables: Public interface sketch for new modules
acceptance_criteria: Each planned runtime module has one owner and one integration point.
Existing MVP modules are reused instead of forked.
The plan clearly separates in-process library calls from future IPC boundaries.
Testing responsibility is assigned per module.
verification: Compare module map against crates/agentd/src modules.
Confirm no task introduces a second policy engine, audit journal, or tool router.
Confirm CLI/TUI tasks depend on AgentCore rather than service-specific workflow code.
risk_notes: Duplicate modules would make security behavior inconsistent across workflows.
